messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the 535.86 driver roll in our nightly infra I'm seeing ~20% throughput regression on the replay harness for T4. Kernel selector is choosing `matmul_generic` instead of the usual `matmul_fast` for a bunch of conv/matmul ops. Anyone seen this?
kevin: saw similar in the 03:00 replay. p50 stable but p95/p99 jump. suspect fallback kernels. can you paste the selector log and the container tag?
maria: paste below. image: `redwood/inference:2026-03-15-cu118`

maria: ```
2026-03-17T03:01:12Z kernelselector INFO selected=matmul_generic reason="no_fast_kernel_for_sm=75"
2026-03-17T03:01:12Z kernelselector INFO chosen_queue=slow_kernels pool=dynamic
```

ash: that `sm=75` hint is interesting — T4 is sm_75. If the vendor driver changed heuristics maybe some fast kernels now claim unsupported. can you attach a short profiler (kernel names + list) e.g. `nvprof --print-gpu-trace`?
maria: pasted lightweight nvprof snippet: `matmul_generic 1.2ms, matmul_fast 0.6ms` but matmul_fast absent on many samples.
kevin: quick try: set `REDWOOD_KERNEL_POLICY=prefer_fast` in env and re-run the replay harness. if throughput recovers it's a selector/heuristic issue not a kernel correctness problem.
ryan: also try the same replay on an A100 image? want to confirm if it's T4-specific or driver-level across archs. I can spin one up real quick.
perf-bot: replay-run summary for 1980012345-run1: workload=chat-stream-96 seq=1024, clients=60, baseline-throughput=980 tok/s, current=780 tok/s, p95 320ms -> 720ms.
maria: thanks, @kevin I set `REDWOOD_KERNEL_POLICY=prefer_fast` and short run shows throughput up to 940 tok/s, p95 down to ~340ms. so selector is the likely culprit.
kevin: good repro. next steps: bisect driver (535.54 vs 535.86) + try newer container with `cuda=11.8` libs pinned/unpinned. also capture `kernelselector.debug` with `--dump-candidate-kernels` for the failing shapes.
ash: create a small reproducer invoking the exact matmul shapes (from replay input). also capture compiler logs: `cuobjdump --dump-sass` for the kernels that used to be fast.
ryan: I'll run A100 check and a two-driver matrix overnight (T4 with 535.54, 535.86; A100 with same drivers) and attach results.
maria: added a short command for the team to run locally: `scripts/replay_harness --shape-file tests/shape-list.json --clients 10 --env REDWOOD_KERNEL_POLICY=prefer_fast --dump-kernelselector > /tmp/ks.log`
kevin: after we have logs, file a perf regression ticket linking the selector logs, nvprof, and the exact container digest. mark priority P1 for Dedicated customers hitting this.
nash: FYI kernel flags we saw toggled in 535.86 release notes: `cuda.dispatcher.enable_fastpaths=false` (suspected). if true that would explain why fast kernels are hidden.
maria: adding to ticket: nightly-run id, raw replay tarball, kernel selector dump. assigning to @kevin + @ash to own the triage.
perf-bot: ticket created: PERF-1429 "T4 throughput drop after driver 535.86 — kernelselector fallback" (linked artifacts: /artifacts/1980012345/replay.tar.gz).
kevin: plan: bisect driver, run `--force-kernel matmul_fast` to confirm correctness, then either ship a selector workaround or recommend pinning driver/container for now.
ryan: will post A100 matrix in morning. tagging #eng-sre for help with driver rollout policy. :eyes: 
maria: thanks all — overnight runs queued. will update thread with final numbers. :thumbsup:
